unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.4 - THEME 2: CLASSROOM LIFE & LEARNING

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will work in groups to design a classroom digital magazine. The magazine will include different sections contributed by each group, such as interviews, photos, research articles, and personal reflections about learning experiences. Each group will use tools like shared documents, databases, timelines, and online platforms to brainstorm ideas, work together, and organise their content. They will need to plan, research, and meet deadlines as a team, confirming that each part of the magazine is well organised and relevant. Through this project, they will practice important teamwork skills, such as sharing files, cooperating with classmates, exchanging ideas, and working together to make group decisions. In the end, each group will present their section of the magazine to the class, highlighting the work they succeeded in it together. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''classroom life and learning with its components such as digital and collaborative projects; student-led class activities; academic skills for learning'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student after prep year 12 of an upper secondary school may know what digital and collaborative projects; student-led class activities; academic skills for learning mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''classroom life and learning'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''classroom life and learning with its components such as digital and collaborative projects; student-led class activities; academic skills for learning'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To write stories about planned and unplanned actions in English by using the target language and vocabulary items. Activity 1: Story Writing The teacher provides students with a prompt: ''Describe a significant event in your life (e.g. a trip, a project, or a memorable moment) where things either went as planned or didn’t. Explain how the event was managed at that time and what happened afterward''. Students write a short story personally by using the target language items. When the stories are completed, students pair up to read and provide constructive feedback on each other’s use of the target language and creativity. Volunteers are invited to share their stories with the whole class by explaining how they integrated the target language into their narratives. The teacher suggests corrections where necessary and engages the class with thought-provoking questions such as: ''Can you identify parts of your story that illustrate the sequence of past events?''. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To understand and to be familiar with planned and unplanned actions in English by using the target vocabulary that is relevant to academic skills, digital projects, and student-led activities. Activity 1: Vocabulary Matching The teacher writes the target vocabulary items on one side of the board and their corresponding definitions or example sentences on the other as arranged in a mixed order. Students work in pairs to match each word with its correct definition or example sentence. After completing the matching activity, students take turns reading aloud each word along with its definition and using it in a sentence that incorporates the target language structures. At the end of the activity, the teacher reviews the answers with the whole class, clarifies any misunderstandings, and provides constructive feedback to enrich students’ comprehension and use of the vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
